lines.text: We left at dawn. I had asked for no fuss. Naturally, the whole village came. And half of Saltmouth. And most of the Skeld.
Take my axe, my lord. The south is full of idiots.
I gave it back. She gave it to Wren. Wren kept it.
My wards gave me a letter. They had written it themselves, in the bathhouse. Six words. Four of them spelled wrong.
It says, please come home soon, Lord Lucan.
Salt, boy. A pinch on your tongue, whenever the south gets too sweet.
Ash said goodbye to Rook, Birk and Tarn, one at a time. Then to their mother, for much longer.
Bring them all back, my lord.
All of them, Bram.
This time, I knew how big that promise was. I made it anyway.
Every mile south, I felt the threads stretch. Long and thin, like spider silk in the wind. But none of them broke.
At the top of the last hill, I looked back. A small grey keep in a green valley, with the white of the Pale behind it. A year ago, it had been thirty-seven people and six goats.
If anyone in Aldcrown laughs at you, can I shoot them?
...We'll see.
The next afternoon, a rider came to Greyhollow wearing my father's colours. He was one day too late.
Bram opened the letter. My father's hand. Short. Cold. Exactly two lines.
Lucan. Whatever they summon you for, do not come.
Bram stood on the south road until dark, holding it.
Far to the south, beneath the Cathedral of the Seven, there was a room that no one was supposed to know about.
In it stood a great stone, glowing like frost under the moon.
And chained to the stone sat a woman, so thin and so still she might have been part of it.
She was humming. A slow, low tune, like wind going round a chimney.
The same song I had hummed to six frightened children. The song I never learned.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. End of season one. Chapter sixty-one, coming soon.
